newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan banks seen cutting long-term prime next week.
newsitem.headline: Japan banks seen cutting long-term prime next week.

text.p: Japan's three long-term credit banks are likely to cut their long-term prime rates and debenture coupons in their monthly revision early next week, market sources said on Monday.
The prime rate, which is the rate at which the banks lend to their most creditworthy customers, has been set at 3.0 percent since September.

The size of the cut is likely to be around 0.3 percentage point, judging from current market conditions, bond traders said. The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ) is likely to announce its revision next Monday.
The other two, the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd (LTCB) and Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB), are expected to follow suit on Tuesday.
The IBJ customarily sets its long-term prime rate 0.9 percentage point above that of its debenture coupon rate. The other two banks adopt the same prime rate.
The yield of the latest IBJ debentures with a 2.1 percent coupon, issued in September, stood at around 1.8 percent on Monday, traders said.
